A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARM–EBM study. The text, equations, five figures and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison. The shorter bibliography in v3 removes duplication without losing unique references.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original synthetic experiments comparing Transformer ARMs and EBMs, including loss convergence, logit distances and KL divergence.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the original synthetic experiments and their results in Figures 2–5.

M1.justification: The ARM–EBM mapping, architectures and learning procedures are unchanged. The added KL-minimization expression on page 4 explicitly restates the existing distillation formulation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic sequence-modeling tasks using Zipfian and normal-softargmax target distributions in Appendix C. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The empirical comparisons retain the same causal Transformer ARM and noncausal Transformer EBM models. No comparison method is added or removed from Figures 2–5.

E3.justification: Appendix C retains the same sequence spaces, model configurations, exact-risk computation, Adam schedule, learning-rate selection and metrics. Figure 5 still evaluates KL(EBM || ARM), despite the reordered theoretical bound.

E4.justification: Figures 3–5 retain the same analyses across model sizes, vocabulary/sequence-length configurations and target distributions, including the relationship between KL divergence and logit distance.

E5.justification: The plotted traces and shading are identical. Neither version supplies run or seed counts, confidence-interval procedures or significance tests, and no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The results plotted in Figures 2–5 are identical. Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same findings about convergence, mapped logits and small KL despite large logit distances for peaked targets.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 reverses Proposition 3 and its Transformer consequence from KL(EBM || ARM) to KL(ARM || EBM), preserving the bound and explicitly stating that both directions satisfy it. Appendix B.4 only partially reverses the proof: its chain-rule expectation and final right-hand KL retain the old ordering, introducing inconsistent equalities. Other theoretical content is unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about the ARM–EBM bijection, equivalence of supervised-learning minima, distillation guarantees and lookahead capabilities.

C2.justification: The interpretations of teacher forcing and lookahead, and the optimization and approximation limitations in Sections 6–7, are unchanged. Appendix C.5 retains its explanation of logit-distance behavior for concentrated distributions.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical Flax-style implementation sketches, architecture details, target-distribution construction and optimization settings. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The removed bibliography block exactly duplicates the retained references. All unique cited works and the research positioning in Section 6 remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes reference-distribution notation, explicitly displays the existing distillation objective, adds a short KL-asymmetry clarification and removes the duplicated References block. These are localized editorial changes.

P2.justification: The added equation and clarification locally reflow pages 4 and 7, while removing the repeated bibliography changes the layout and appendix pagination. All five figures, their captions and graphical content are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the distillation objective and removes a duplicated bibliography, but its partial KL reversal introduces incorrect equalities into Appendix B.4, where v2 kept the argument order consistent. The new proof equates opposite KL directions and retains expectations under the wrong distribution for the revised expression. This localized loss of proof correctness outweighs the modest presentation gains. The bound remains obtainable by consistently applying the existing lemma and chain rule, limiting the deterioration.
